title: Dust-Covered Pearl
subtitle: She has been silent for far too long.

items.text: *drip-drip-drip*

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Willow, I think the water's been shut off.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I opened it all the way, but nothing's coming out.
Flutterpage tilts her head as she brings it in close and sticks her little finger into the faucet, feeling only a few drips of water.
*drip-drip-drip*
Dangling in midair, Willow wipes the beads of sweat from her face.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Go to the water resource office, and ask the staff what's going on. If they're not there, they're probably at the Gin Barrel.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I know you want me to leave, but how're you goin' to track the time and score without me?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Hmph.
*drip-drip-drip*

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: With a heart that's pure, and a body lean, to the hunt I go, through forest green.
Her wand unexpectedly slips from her left hand and plummets to the floor.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Feck. Pick it up and keep going, Charlotte.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: The movement's correct. First spin, then run the geranium over the shoulder, let it slide down the back, and as it falls to the ground, step on it to hop into the air, then ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Sulis, Sulis, all life's offerings I bring, as sacrifice to you, from the growing spring ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Ack! This is all wrong!
She halts, wrinkling her brow.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: The flow needs to be smoother.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Alright, let's try this again.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: The sprouting light within the world's egg lays ...
*thud* She gracefully descends from the air, her mechanical prosthesis squeaking softly as she lands.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hooray! You did it!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: This element requires a 720-degree turn. I haven't even made it to 600.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oh ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Once more from the beginning.
*drip-drip-drip*

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Your endless quest brings parents' joyful days.
*thud* Her body has collapsed on this rotted wooden floor countless times today, and with the setting sun, each fall feels heavier than the last.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: How 'bout this time?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I did it.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: You did what?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I completed the element. I did it.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Blimey!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: So you mean, you did that-that move you've always talked about?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: The two-and-a-half turn with free leg backwards and upwards, wand throw and catch.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Does that mean you can complete the ritual, too?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Yes.
Willow examines the geranium in her hand, the tender pink leaves quietly resting in her palm.
Not a single petal has fallen or been harmed in any way.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Alright. That's enough for today.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: It's supper time. Your mother must be waiting for you to come home with beef stew, fried fish, and bread.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But why? You usually train for about three more hours.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Not today. I need a break. *yawn* I'm totally exhausted.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hmm.
Flutterpage stays exactly where she is, showing no desire to move.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Why are you still standing there? Do I need to get His Majesty's limousine to pick you up?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oh, I get it. If I don't leave now, the critters in the garden will bite my ears.
She mumbles on to herself as she quickly makes her way to the door.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Good, I won't see you off.
A gust of wind blows in through the door as Flutterpage makes her exit. With a flick of Willow's wand, she slams it shut behind her.
The room settles back into its muted, oppressive stillness.
*drip-drip-drip*
Willow steps into the pale yellow light of the kitchen and shuts the door behind her.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Ack, bloody!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You filthy little stain! Who ever gave you permission to stick to my cauldron?!
Willow sits beside the sink, absorbed in cleaning her cauldron.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: *pant* Look at me! I have a whole sink of dishes that haven't washed, and here I am, fighting a little stain on a cauldron, and when the water's just shut off, too!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I did ask Buzzie to visit the water resource office. Hopefully it didn't slip her mind, if she even knows how to use it.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Never mind. I can clean it off without water.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: *pant* Hah!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Got it! It's off!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You stubborn little thing. Everyone loathes you, avoids you like the plague. You're just a pathetic little stain, clinging to what you can.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Do you have no shame? To sully the sacred floor with your artificial leg!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: So what if you finished the element?!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: It won't bring back your leg! Without it, you're no different from a clown! How could you possibly compete again?! You're not qualified!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: No, I'm not.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: All the money I spent on this leg, all the efforts I made to finish the ritual, they're utterly pointless!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: When was the last time I ate dessert? Or even a chip, for that matter? Year after year, I've trained harder than the last to make up for my leg, but what's the point?
She flings the scrubbing brush into the cauldron, and her heavy breathing gradually slows down.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Heh, forget it. Everything will be alright.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Just give up. Stop thinking about it. Stop hoping. Don't look back or ahead.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Just look at the cauldron.
Beneath the dim light, Willow raises her now sparkling clean cauldron to eye level.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: See how clean it is now? Stop clinging to places where you don't belong.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: The world is perfect without you.
The rusted faucet suddenly sputters out a blast of water. It splashes across the counter, startling Willow.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Ah!
Willow leaps back with the reflexes of a true athlete. Her gaze quickly falls on the piece of paper on the table.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: No!
She dashes forward, snatching the paper away from the raging spray of water.
It's the registration form for the Uluru London Qualifiers.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: *panting*
Her hands, clutching the form, begin to tremble. Before long, the tremors have engulfed her entire body.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Still intact.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Hahahahaha.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Still ... intact.
Caroline stands at the center of the sports field in her training gear, feeling the fiery pulse of the ground beneath her feet.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hey.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Bartley! I finally found you!

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: F-Flutterpage? Is that you? I can hardly open my eyes in all this wind. Where, where are you?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I'm right here!
The wind subsides as Flutterpage makes a hurried landing, nearly losing her balance.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: You've been looking for me, have you? How did you find me?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I knew where you were stayin' in London, but you wasn't there when I arrived. Then, the landlady, Erika, told me to try the trainin' field. Looks like she was right.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: She was. I've been training here every day. You know, to settle in before the event.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Good luck, then. Actually, I've come here to deliver a very important and urgent letter to you. Here.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: "A Letter of Challenge"?
The bold, crooked letters scrawled across the top proudly proclaim the letter's importance.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: "I, Liberti Grove, on behalf of Charlotte O'Hagan, hereby challenge Caroline Bartley to see who'll become the champion of the Floor Ritual in the Uluru Games."

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: "No matter if you're a seeded player, a champion, or the sun you say you are ..."

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: "Charlotte O'Hagan, the only Floor Ritualist to master the two-and-a-half turn with free leg backwards and upwards, wand throw and catch ..."

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: "... will defeat you and win first place in the London Qualifiers!"

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: You mean ...
